why: One registry for what the exported tree is checked with and by what. Generated by bin/ops/export-core-registry.php from nativa-php-core: the gates it carries are the exported Makefile's targets, and a tool is kept only when its pin resolves in this tree. Read by `make gates`.

tools.name: mago
tools.why: lint and guard are gates, analyze is a reading, format is excluded; see docs/mago-evaluation.md

gates.answers: does every tracked .php file outside vendor/ parse (php -l) — kernel and catalogue
does the tree behave (PHPUnit: tests/ plus modules/*/tests/)
types (phpstan level 9), language rewrites (rector dry) and style (cs-fixer dry) over the kernel
the curated lint rules, ceiling zero, over kernel and catalogue
does a kernel file name a module, inline FQCNs included
the catalogue alone: lint + analyze, never a gate
does every catalogued module install in closure order (refuses a cycle)
does the booted panel walk its admin flows over HTTP on temp databases
does a clean clone build a green artifact
do the three deployment-profile branches answer skip / skip / fail
builds the theme bundles in-tree (pnpm workspace under Frontend/packages)
no tracked .env and no secret-shaped literal in tracked code
no high/critical advisories in composer.lock or the pnpm lockfile
prints this registry: every pin, every gate and the question it answers
which targets exist, grouped by section
are the PHP dev dependencies installed (the kernel runtime has none)
all four Mago tools over the phpstan scope, informational
